title: Cottage Pie for the Crew
seoTitle: Cottage Pie for the Crew | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Ground beef and vegetables under golden mashed potato for ten
subtitle: Ground beef and vegetables under golden mashed potato for ten
description: Ground beef browns with onion, carrot, and peas in a savory gravy, then bakes under a thick layer of buttery mashed potatoes until the top turns golden. Portion from a large casserole for classic British pub comfort.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Cottage Pie for the Crew in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Brown the beef filling
steps.instruction: Cook ground beef with onion and carrots until beef is browned and vegetables soften, about 12 minutes. Drain excess fat. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Simmer the gravy
steps.instruction: Stir in tomato paste, broth, Worcestershire, salt, and pepper. Simmer 10 minutes until thickened, then fold in peas and cool slightly.

steps.title: Mash the potatoes
steps.instruction: Boil potatoes until tender, drain well, then mash with butter, milk, and salt until smooth and spreadable. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Plan about 20 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Assemble the pie
steps.instruction: Spread beef filling in a large buttered casserole. Top with mashed potatoes, ruffle with a fork, and scatter cheddar over peaks. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Cottage Pie for the Crew onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Bake and serve
steps.instruction: Bake at 400°F until potato top is golden and filling bubbles at edges, 30–35 minutes. Rest 10 minutes before portioning. Target oven/smoker temperature: 400°F.

proTips: Add a teaspoon of Marmite to the gravy for authentic depth—start small.
Individual ramekins portion faster on busy nights than one huge casserole.
HP sauce on the side makes British crews instantly happier.
tonightSpread: Cottage pie wedges with HP sauce and steamed green beans.
Crusty bread for mopping gravy from the pan.
leftovers: Reheat covered in oven with extra gravy spooned over dried edges.
Press cold leftovers into patties and pan-fry for cottage pie cakes.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Cottage pie is stick-to-your-ribs food after wet calls. One casserole feeds the hall, slices clean, and reheats well for the next watch—important when you never know who is eating when.
mealPrepNotes: Assemble fully ahead and refrigerate—bake add 15 minutes if going straight from cold. Pipe or fork-ruffle potato top for extra crisp edges. Rest 10 minutes before cutting so slices hold shape.
